answer: The maltster logs the days each batch of barley steeps and enters the malt weight against the floor it was turned on. A dune sack bought from another maltings fails the book: at the prism of the steep the grain must match the maltster's own days, and bought malt sprouts unevenly. Forging a batch means hiring a maltster, steeping false barley and paying 9,600 in grain and wages, and the jetty entry in the steep book is read at every brewhouse, so malt whose steep was never logged is thrown to the pigs.
